proposals.before: The reading runs, 『Kings take it as ill-omened; the sovereign's life is unbounded; a ruler is displaced; one may become king in his stead; the realm changes its dynastic reckoning.』
proposals.after: The reading runs, 『Kings take it as ill-omened; the sovereign's allotted fate has no set term; a ruler is displaced; one may become king in his stead; the realm changes its dynastic reckoning.』
proposals.reason: 主命無期 means the ruler's mandate or lifespan has no secure term (is in jeopardy), not that life is unbounded.

proposals.after: In the second year of Jianyuan, ninth month, jiawu new moon: the sun was eclipsed.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English sentence is ungrammatically lowercased at the start of a new unit.

proposals.before: In the second month of year 6, on the renchen jia watch, the thirteenth jia watch, and the fifteenth jia watch, the moon each time haloed Taiwei.
proposals.after: In the second month of year 6, on the renxu jia watch, the thirteenth jia watch, and the fifteenth jia watch, the moon each time haloed Taiwei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 壬戌 is the sexagenary date renxu, not renchen (壬辰).

proposals.before: Year 6, second month—on nights of renchen-jia, the thirteenth jia night, and the fifteenth jia night, the moon all showed halos encompassing Taiwei.
proposals.after: Year 6, second month—on nights of renxu-jia, the thirteenth jia night, and the fifteenth jia night, the moon all showed halos encompassing Taiwei.
proposals.reason: Chinese 壬戌 is renxu; the literal English wrongly transliterates it as renchen.

proposals.before: Eighth month, on renshen, the moon stood in the Net, three cun northwest of the second star of the left thigh.
proposals.after: Eighth month, on renshen, the moon stood in the Net and encroached three cun northwest of the second star of the left thigh.
proposals.reason: Chinese 犯 records an encroachment on the left-thigh star; the idiomatic English only locates the moon northwest and omits that transit verb.

proposals.before: Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the secondary prime minister star below Room's northern head—an encroachment.
proposals.after: Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the second minister star at Room's northern head—an encroachment.
proposals.reason: Chinese 房北頭第二次相星 names the second-minister star of Room's northern head; 次相 is not a star located 'below' the head.

proposals.before: Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the secondary prime minister star below the northern head of Room, counted as encroachment.
proposals.after: Seventh month, on yiyou, the moon entered eight cun northwest of the second minister star at the northern head of Room, counted as encroachment.
proposals.reason: Chinese 房北頭第二次相星 names the second-minister star of Room's northern head; 次相 is not a star located 'below' the head.

proposals.before: On bingchen the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at Room's northern end, encroaching.
proposals.after: On bingshen the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at Room's northern end, encroaching.
proposals.reason: Source date 丙申 is bingshen; bingchen would be 丙辰.

proposals.before: On bingchen, the moon stood one chi north of the chief minister star at the northern end of Room, encroaching.

proposals.before: September, on yichou—the moon occulted Lead Ox's south star.
proposals.after: Ninth month, on yichou, the moon occulted Ox Leader's south star.
proposals.reason: 九月 is a lunar ninth month, not Gregorian September, and 牽牛 is Ox Leader, not Lead Ox.

proposals.after: Ninth month, on gengyin—the moon traveled six cun southwest of the Weeping Star, an encroachment.

decisions.reason: In this ill-omened reading, 主命無期 means the ruler's mandate or allotted span has no secure term, matching 有徙主 and 天下更紀; 'life is unbounded' reverses that sense.
The unit is a standalone sentence opening the eclipse series; the lowercased start is ungrammatical, and prefixing In matches neighboring dated entries without changing meaning.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建元二年九月甲午朔，日蝕。

decisions.reason: The unit begins a new sentence and must be capitalized; adding In restores grammar without altering 建元四年七月戊辰 or 危宿.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 建元四年七月戊辰，月在危宿蝕。

decisions.reason: The date graph is 壬戌 (renxu); renchen would require 壬辰, so the original sexagenary name is wrong.
The same 壬戌 must be romanized renxu in the literal field; renchen misidentifies the day.
The source verb is 犯, a recorded encroachment on the Net's left-thigh star; locating the moon three cun northwest without that verb omits the omen.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 月在畢，犯左股第二星西北三寸

decisions.reason: 房北頭第二次相星 names the 次相 star at Room's northern head; 次相 is the second-minister title, not a star placed 'below' the head.
The literal field repeats the same invented 'below'; 次相 is the star-title at 房北頭, so 'at the northern head of Room' is the accurate locative.
The source day is 丙申 (bingshen), consecutive after 乙未; bingchen would be 丙辰 and is not in the text.
The literal date must follow 丙申 as bingshen; bingchen is a different sexagenary day.
牽牛 is the Ox Leader lodge; nearby units already use Ox Leader for the same asterism, while Lead Ox is a conflicting invented name.
九月 is the lunar ninth month, not Gregorian September, and 牽牛 should be Ox Leader, not Lead Ox.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 九月乙丑，月掩牽牛南星。

decisions.reason: 九月 is the ninth lunar month of the chronicle; rendering it as September imports a Gregorian month the source does not use.
泰 is tài, so 泰元 romanizes as Taiyuan; Taoyuan does not match the graph 泰.
The literal field likewise misreads 泰元 as Taoyuan; Taiyuan is the correct transcription of 泰元.
